advisor_identified: Timothy D. Hall, historian of early America at Central Michigan University, later professor of history and dean at Samford University.

doctorate.title: Contested Boundaries: Itinerancy and the Reshaping of the Colonial American Religious World

evidence.says: Samford's May 6, 2016 appointment announcement identifies Timothy D. Hall as a Central Michigan history faculty member since 1993 and states that he earned his doctorate in American history at Northwestern University in 1991.
Northwestern's 2017 History Department newsletter, printed page 15, lists alumnus Tim Hall (PhD 1991) as dean and professor of history at Samford University.
Timothy D. Hall's scholarly society profile identifies him with Central Michigan University, gives PhD, Northwestern University, 1991, and lists his book Contested Boundaries.

A dissertation bibliography preserved in Virginia Tech's repository, printed page 259, cites Timothy David Hall's Contested Boundaries: Itinerancy and the Reshaping of the Colonial American Religious World as a Northwestern University PhD dissertation, 1991.
Duke University Press attributes the 1994 book of the same title to Timothy D. Hall and identifies him as assistant professor of early American history at Central Michigan University.

notes: Institution, year and dissertation title match the linked AHA record. The title is corroborated by a scholarly bibliography rather than a directly accessed thesis catalogue. The supplied student entries omit university names; all three individual supervisions were not independently verified.
